plannedCharts.title: The poverty rate changes when the poverty line changes
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank Poverty & Equity Brief · poverty headcount rates, not dollars · lines are $3/day and $4.20/day in 2021 PPP
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The strongest version of the good news is true at the lowest line; the broader poverty line still leaves nearly a quarter of India below it.

plannedCharts.title: The next floor is much more crowded
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank Poverty & Equity Brief + WDI/PIP · $3, $4.20 and $8.30 poverty lines in 2021 PPP, 2022-23
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: India-scale turns small percentages into large populations, and the upper-middle-income line shows how far 'secure' is from 'above extreme poverty'.

plannedCharts.title: Poverty gaps show depth, not just headcount
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank WDI/PIP · poverty gap at $3, $4.20 and $8.30 lines, 2021 PPP · latest 2022
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A headcount only says how many people are below a line; the poverty gap says how far below the line they are on average.

plannedCharts.title: At the $4.20 line, rural poverty is still higher
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank Poverty & Equity Brief · poverty headcount rate at the lower-middle-income line, 2021 PPP
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Both rural and urban poverty fell, but the rural rate remains nearly twice the urban rate at the broader line.

plannedCharts.title: The broader line is crowded with children and low-education households
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank Poverty & Equity Brief · group poverty rates at the lower-middle-income line, 2022-23
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The remaining poor are not evenly spread across age and education.

plannedCharts.title: India's last official poverty line stopped here
plannedCharts.subtitle: Planning Commission · official Tendulkar poverty estimates · NSS consumption rounds
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: India's last adopted national poverty estimate is still the 2011-12 Tendulkar number: 21.9%. Every newer claim is an estimate under another method.

plannedCharts.title: A higher line counted more people as poor
plannedCharts.unit: % of people below the committee line
plannedCharts.subtitle: Planning Commission press note + Rangarajan Expert Group · poverty headcount rates for the same year, 2011-12
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The famous poverty-line fight is not abstract. Rangarajan's higher standard raises the all-India poverty estimate from 21.9% to 29.5% in the same year.

plannedCharts.title: What the old poverty line meant in rupees
plannedCharts.subtitle: Planning Commission press note + Rangarajan Expert Group · monthly per-capita poverty lines, 2011-12
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The official line was low enough to make the political controversy obvious: about Rs 816 per person per month in rural India and Rs 1,000 in urban India.

plannedCharts.title: A serious dissent says the post-2011 fall was much slower
plannedCharts.subtitle: Tinbergen Institute Discussion Paper 2025-069/V · PLFS-imputed Tendulkar-compatible poverty estimates, Table 5
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: This is the strongest methodological counterweight to simple HCES comparisons: it adjusts for survey non-comparability using imputation.

plannedCharts.title: The consumption floor has risen
plannedCharts.subtitle: MoSPI HCES · average monthly per-capita consumption, current prices, without imputation
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Rising MPCE is the direct consumption-side reason poverty estimates fell after 2011-12.

plannedCharts.title: Free welfare items matter to measured consumption
plannedCharts.subtitle: MoSPI HCES · average MPCE with imputed value of free welfare items
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Free food and other transfers raise what poor households consume, and HCES now counts that value explicitly.

plannedCharts.title: The bottom rung is still thin
plannedCharts.subtitle: MoSPI HCES 2023-24 · average rural MPCE by fractile class
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The average can look comfortable while the poorest 5% of rural India spends only Rs 1,677 per person per month.

plannedCharts.title: The poorest half gets about a third of rural consumption
plannedCharts.subtitle: MoSPI HCES 2023-24 · rural consumption share by group, computed from HCES tables
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Poverty is a threshold story; this shows the distribution around it.

plannedCharts.title: Choose a monthly MPCE cutoff, get a different headcount
plannedCharts.unit: % of people below the chosen cutoff
plannedCharts.subtitle: Computed from HCES 2023-24 unit-level microdata · nominal monthly MPCE cutoffs, calibrated to published rural/urban means
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: This lets readers test the sensitivity directly: poverty is not a natural fact; it changes with the monthly consumption cutoff we choose.

plannedCharts.title: Below Rs 3,000 MPCE, the state ranking changes sharply
plannedCharts.subtitle: Computed from HCES 2023-24 unit-level microdata · Rs 3,000 nominal monthly MPCE cutoff
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The sensitivity test is not evenly distributed: the same rupee floor produces very different headcounts across states.

plannedCharts.title: The map changes the poverty story
plannedCharts.subtitle: MoSPI HCES 2023-24 · average rural MPCE by major state
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Rural Kerala's average MPCE is more than twice rural Chhattisgarh's. A national poverty line hides that regional gap.

plannedCharts.title: Below Rs 3,000 MPCE, ST and SC households are most exposed
plannedCharts.subtitle: Computed from HCES 2023-24 unit-level microdata · Rs 3,000 nominal monthly MPCE cutoff by household-head social group
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Average caste gaps become starker when translated into a below-cutoff headcount.

plannedCharts.title: Poverty risk still runs along caste
plannedCharts.subtitle: Computed from HCES 2023-24 unit-level microdata · average MPCE by social group of household head
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The consumption ladder is not socially neutral: Scheduled Tribe and Scheduled Caste households sit far below the 'Others' average.

plannedCharts.title: NITI's MPI is a deprivation index, not a cash poverty line
plannedCharts.subtitle: NITI Aayog · National MPI headcount · 2005-06 is NFHS-3 baseline; 2013-14 and 2022-23 are estimated points
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The non-cash evidence also shows a large fall: deprivation across health, education and living standards has come down sharply.

plannedCharts.title: The global MPI adds intensity and vulnerability
plannedCharts.subtitle: OPHI/UNDP Global MPI Country Briefing 2023 · India, NFHS/DHS 2019-21
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The global MPI gives extra texture: how deprived the MPI poor are, who is vulnerable, and the rural-urban split.

plannedCharts.title: MPI by state confirms the geography of deprivation
plannedCharts.subtitle: NITI Aayog National MPI 2023 · state headcount ratios from NFHS-5, 2019-21
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The regional story is visible outside consumption too: the high-deprivation states are not random.

plannedCharts.title: The basic household floor rose, but health cover still lags
plannedCharts.subtitle: NFHS-6 (2023-24) · latest India totals; denominators differ by indicator
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A poverty article needs to show what the welfare state and household capabilities have actually built.

plannedCharts.title: Nutrition is the hard caveat
plannedCharts.subtitle: NFHS-6 (2023-24) · selected nutrition indicators, latest India totals
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: No poverty article should declare victory while child stunting, wasting, underweight and inadequate diets remain this high.

plannedCharts.title: Basic services improved, but deprivation did not vanish
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank Poverty & Equity Brief · multidimensional poverty components, 2022-23
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Electricity deprivation is near zero, but sanitation and schooling deprivations still show up at meaningful levels.

plannedCharts.title: A hospital bill can still push households back down
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank UHC financial-protection indicators · latest India observations, mostly 2022
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Poverty is not only crossing a line; it is also whether a household can survive a health shock without falling back.

plannedCharts.title: Having work is not the same as being secure
plannedCharts.subtitle: ILOSTAT · working poverty rate, employed people below international poverty line
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The last poverty layer is vulnerability: a household can work and still be close to the line.
